key_insight: DEFEAT enables gradient-based crystal design by jointly optimizing elemental composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports targeted searches for superconductors and photovoltaic absorbers while incorporating an energy penalty to favor stability.
method: Extend a pretrained EquiformerV3 model to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Combine gradients from fine-tuned property models with a machine-learned energy penalty.
Validate candidates with first-principles calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition.
evidence_signal: DFPT predicts Allen–Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39 of 45 novel designs, peaking at 24.0 K; SCAN confirms ten novel absorber structures within 20% of the 1.34 eV target on raw or corrected scales and within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective, and finite-temperature phase competition can reorder static-hull rankings.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
